source.title: Monotonic Learning in the PAC Framework: A New Perspective
source.authors: Ming Li; Chenyi Zhang; Qin Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper argues for monotonic error improvement with increasing sample size and reports its own sample-size experiments, refining or challenging the more-data-can-hurt claim in the tested settings.
record.gate_note: The study varies training sample size, not model size or training epochs. It does not identify or test an interpolation threshold. Its PAC-derived theoretical distributions are bounds, not empirical test-error measurements.
record.test_reason: The paper proves that PAC-derived risk-bound distributions are monotone in sample size. It also shows decreasing empirical error curves on three classical tasks. Double descent appears only as cited related work (Belkin et al. peaking at an interpolation threshold). V3 is conditional on being near the interpolation threshold. Every sweep here runs far past capacity, for example VC dimension 1 with m ≥ 200 and VC dimension 5 with m ≥ 200. The sweeps therefore cannot show whether more data hurts near a threshold. The monotone curves are a different finding: monotonicity of ERM learners in PAC-learnable classes well past capacity. They are not evidence against V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors prove that PAC-derived risk distributions are monotone for ERM learners when H is finite or has finite VC dimension. Their experiments show empirical error improving with sample size, with the theoretical distributions as conservative estimates that converge to the minimum error. The conclusion says 'two' problems, although three were run.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PAC sample-complexity bounds and sample-size sweeps on classical learning problems rather than model-size or training-time sweeps in deep networks; no interpolation-threshold analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The sample-size schedule differs by task: m = 25 × iterations for Boolean conjunction and m = 200 × iterations for the threshold and Iris tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical mean generalization error decreases with sample size on Boolean conjunction (96% of steps decreasing), threshold, and Iris SVM tasks. All sample sizes are well beyond capacity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For ERM learners on finite-H or finite-VC problems, sampled well past capacity, expected error decreases monotonically with sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: PAC-derived theoretical error distributions shift toward lower error with sample size, stay to the right of the empirical distributions, and merge with them at large m.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PAC-bound-derived risk distributions are monotone and conservative relative to empirical error distributions.

record.problems: The experiments cover three classical tasks, not deep networks or model-size and epoch sweeps; they do not locate an interpolation threshold. The Boolean-task monotonicity is reported with a 96% probability and also described as having a few upward fluctuations. No confidence intervals or error bars are stated. The theoretical distributions are risk bounds rather than empirical test-error measurements. The conclusion refers to experiments on two problems, although the body also reports an Iris experiment.

untested.parts: The near-interpolation-threshold regime is never sampled. All sample sizes far exceed hypothesis-class capacity.

record.verdict_notes: The record linked R1–R3 to V3 and labelled them challenges. That overstates the bearing: V3 is explicitly about the near-interpolation-threshold regime, which these sweeps never approach. The paper itself frames double descent only as related work. The Iris sample sizes exceed the two-class dataset size without explanation.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or deep-network experiment.
The experiments vary sample size and report error trends, but do not locate or test an interpolation threshold or establish that any tested setting is near one.
No capacity sweep through an interpolation point across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, or sample size.
No noise or regularization dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization is tested.
No comparison with an effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: Boolean literal conjunction problem; positive-example learning algorithm
rows.operation_detail: Increase training sample size across 50 iterations; assess empirical generalization-error distributions
rows.measure: Mean of empirical error distribution Pm; generalization error computed against ground truth
rows.value: Monotonically decreasing trend with a probability of 96% over 50 iterations; the plotted curves have few upward fluctuations.
rows.note: The reported trend is downward as sample size increases; the paper does not state that this experiment is near an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Realizable finite-H conjunction learner that always returns a consistent hypothesis. There is no interpolation-threshold regime in the sweep, so V3's near-threshold effect cannot appear. The mean decreases on 96% of successive steps, with a few upward fluctuations. The 'reversed' state against V3 is unwarranted.

rows.subject: Threshold function learning problem; threshold candidate algorithm
rows.operation_detail: Increase training sample size and assess empirical generalization-error distributions
rows.measure: Empirical error distribution Pm and its learning curve
rows.value: The paper reports similar results to the Boolean conjunction experiment and describes the learning curves as appearing monotone; Figure 6(a) plots the mean.
rows.note: The text does not give a numerical trend or identify an interpolation threshold for this task.
rows.check: Threshold functions with VC dimension 1, starting at m = 200. This is far beyond any sample-size threshold, so the row cannot test V3. No numbers are given, only that the curves appear monotone.

rows.subject: Iris Versicolor and Iris Virginica classification; SVM
rows.operation_detail: Increase training sample size and assess empirical generalization-error distributions
rows.measure: Empirical error distribution Pm and its learning curve
rows.value: The paper reports similar results to the other tasks and describes the learning curves as appearing monotone; Figure 8(a) plots the mean.
rows.note: The text does not give a numerical trend or identify an interpolation threshold for this task.
rows.check: SVM with VC dimension treated as 5, starting at m = 200. This is far beyond the threshold. The two Iris classes contain only 100 examples, yet m runs up to 10,000, and the text does not explain how such samples were drawn. No numbers are given for this task.

rows.value: The theoretical distributions shift toward lower error as sample size increases and are described as monotonically decreasing.
rows.locator: Sections 4.2 and Analysis on the results; Figures 3 and 4(a)
rows.note: A theoretical bound is not an empirical test-error measurement, so this row is not linked to a claim version.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: The three tested PAC-learning tasks over their reported sample-size sweeps
reader_labels.reason: The empirical error curves are described as decreasing or appearing monotone as sample size grows (R1–R3); none is reported to show an increase. The experiments do not establish that these settings are near an interpolation threshold.
